text:
maria: Heads up — compliance flagged a permission grant in prod at 2026-03-15T10:45:21Z where the audit event shows principalEmail=null but serviceName indicates our roles-reconciler. Need to figure out who actually triggered this and why the actor is missing. cc @june
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: permission.grant on resource projects/redwood-prod/serviceAccounts/admin at 2026-03-15T10:45:21Z. event_id=evt_0x9c7, actor=null, service=roles-reconciler. Link: https://internal-logs/ui/event/evt_0x9c7
samir: Can you paste the raw audit JSON for that event? quick thought: KMS key rotation or log-redaction could have stripped the principal.
maria: Pasting the snippet from log storage (redacted for PII but shows the null actor):
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-03-15T10:45:21Z",
  "eventId": "evt_0x9c7",
  "serviceName": "roles-reconciler@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
  "principalEmail": null,
  "requestMetadata": {"callerIp": "10.4.5.6"},
  "authorizationInfo": [{"permission": "resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy", "granted": true}],
  "protoPayload": {"methodName": "SetIamPolicy", "resource": "projects/redwood-prod"}
}
```
dave: That matches the old symptom we saw when the logshipper redaction kicked in during KMS envelope key rotations. The service shows up but principalEmail null — our rehydration step failed for short-lived tokens. We noted this in the last ops-oncall runbook but it slipped through.
samir: If the reconciler ran with a short-lived token derived from KMS-wrapped creds, the log producer may not have the principal at write time. We should join the audit events with the reconciler job logs to recover the job-run identity. Quick bq suggestion:
```sql
-- join GCP audit logs with our reconciler job traces to map job_id -> event_id
SELECT a.eventId, a.timestamp, r.job_id, r.start_time, r.triggered_by
FROM `redwood-prod.audit_logs` a
LEFT JOIN `redwood-prod.role_reconciler.runs` r
  ON a.protoPayload.requestId = r.request_id
WHERE a.eventId = 'evt_0x9c7' OR a.timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(TIMESTAMP('2026-03-15T10:45:21Z'), INTERVAL 10 MINUTE) AND TIMESTAMP_ADD(TIMESTAMP('2026-03-15T10:45:21Z'), INTERVAL 10 MINUTE)
```
june: Compliance needs an authoritative CSV with who/what/when for that window (10:30-10:50Z) and an explanation for the missing principal. Can you export it and tag SOC2? Need by EOD.
maria: I'll run the export now. @dave can you confirm whether a KMS rotation or key version flip happened around 10:39Z? If so, that could explain the gap.
dave: Confirmed: we rotated KMS key rk-main at 2026-03-15T10:39:12Z as part of a scheduled rotation. There was a ~6 minute window where the token rewrap path returned tokens without the principal field to the log agent. Ops is already rerunning the logshipper reingest with --rehydrate-principals; ETA ~45m.
samir: Recommendation: add a deterministic header from the reconciler (X-Job-Id and X-Initiator) so even if principalEmail is lost, the request contains a stable caller_id we can trust. I'll open a tiny PR and add it to the reconciler runbook.
maria: Thanks. Action items: (1) export CSV and attach to SOC2 tracker (owner: maria) (2) PR for X-Job-Id header + runbook update (owner: samir) (3) reingest logs with rehydrate (owner: dave). I'll document timeline in the postmortem doc.
june: Received. Please mark the CSV and the postmortem entry in the compliance tracker (SOC2-2026-Q1). If reingestion doesn't recover the principal, we may need a compensating control note in the report.
maria: Noted — I'll include a compensating-controls section if needed. Will post the exported CSV link here once ready. :thumbsup:
